Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.8% today to close at $371.81, extending a solid two-week gain of 3.8%. The move reflects multiple tailwinds for refiners: oil prices jumped overnight after U.S. strikes on Iranian targets pushed Brent crude above $90 a barrel, geopolitical tensions in Ukraine threaten Russian energy supplies, and refineries are already running at 97.4% capacity — near maximum — which tightens the supply of refined products like gasoline and diesel. When crude gets expensive and refinery capacity is scarce, refiners typically capture wider margins on what they produce.

The White House's signal that it plans to work with U.S. refiners on boosting capacity also signals potential political support for the industry, which may have encouraged buying by investors who see tailwinds ahead.
